A quick guide on how to get started blogging with [Quarto](https://quarto.org/).

**1. Install Quarto**

The official documentation recommends installing Quarto with a `.deb` package, which puts the binaries into a system-level folder. Since I didn't have root access on my [Solveit](https://solve.it.com/) instance, I discovered I could install Quarto via `pip`, which downloads the binaries into the user's Python environment.
```python
!pip install quarto-cli
!quarto --version
```

**2. Create a Quarto blog project**

Solveit code cells don't work well with interactive prompts, so I piped the blog title into the command to skip the interactive prompt.
```python
!echo "TIL Blog" | quarto create project blog myblog
```
```python
!ls -la myblog/
```

**3. Publish to GitHub Pages**

This was the most involved part. I mostly followed the [Quarto documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages.html#publish-command) for publishing on GitHub Pages, along with some help from Solveit.

- Get the GitHub token from Solveit's secrets to authenticate with GitHub.
```python
from os import getenv
token = getenv("GITHUB_TOKEN")
print(len(token))
```

- Create an empty GitHub repo named `til` on github.com.

- Change into the directory where the blog files are stored.
```python
%cd myblog
```

- Add a `.gitignore` to avoid saving the output directory of the project.
```python
with open('.gitignore', 'w') as f:
    f.write('/.quarto/\n/_site/\n')
```

- Initialize the local repo and make the first commit.
```python
!git init
!git add .
!git commit -m "First commit of Quarto blog"
```

- Push to GitHub.
```python
!git remote add origin https://{token}@github.com/angelikawagner/til.git
!git branch -M main
!git push -u origin main
```

- Create a `gh-pages` branch on GitHub.
```python
!git checkout --orphan gh-pages
!git reset --hard
!git commit --allow-empty -m "Initialising gh-pages branch"
!git push origin gh-pages
!git checkout main
```

- Configure GitHub Pages settings. Go to your repo on GitHub → Settings → Pages → set Source to the `gh-pages` branch and directory to `/ (root)`.

- Publish! I used the `--no-browser` flag so it doesn't wait for the website to be available and open a browser window, and the `--no-prompt` flag to avoid the interactive prompt to confirm publish actions.
```python
!quarto publish gh-pages --no-browser --no-prompt
```

**4. Customize the blog**

Now to the fun part! All you need for a new post is to
- Update the post files locally.
- Commit changes and push to GitHub.
- Run the command `!quarto publish gh-pages --no-browser --no-prompt` to publish the changes.
